site.note: Interpreted this as a first-pass audit of the public SQLite website, with UK English Google results for both supplied keywords. HTTPS returned 200 on the non-www host without a host redirect. HTTP and www variants were not separately fetched. Sampled the homepage, About, Documentation and Download pages.

bottom_line: The sampled site is accessible and the homepage is fast: mobile Lighthouse performance 100, SEO 83. The clearest opportunities are missing descriptions on all four pages, missing H1s on three, and recovery of externally linked error URLs reported by the backlink provider. Neither keyword returned sqlite.org in the eight conventional organic results supplied, although the brand query cited SQLite in its AI overview; treat this unusual brand result as a snapshot, not proof of a sustained ranking problem. Start with a small homepage/template patch for descriptive metadata and headings, then investigate broken backlink destinations.

fixes.fix: Add unique meta descriptions to all four sampled pages. Describe SQLite's serverless SQL library on home/About, API and SQL reference material on Documentation, and source/binary downloads on Download. Implement a per-page description field in the template.
fixes.evidence: All four page checks returned description=null and no_description=true (S3–S6). Homepage Lighthouse independently scored meta-description=0.
fixes.why: Gives search engines a relevant snippet option and users a clearer reason to click. Descriptions are not a direct ranking fix and Google may rewrite them.

fixes.fix: Add one descriptive H1 to home and promote the main Documentation and Download headings to H1. Suggested homepage title/H1: 'SQLite — A Serverless, Embedded SQL Database'. Keep About's existing single H1 and avoid keyword repetition.
fixes.evidence: Homepage has no H1 and title 'SQLite Home Page'; Documentation and Download have no H1, with their primary labels at H2 (S3, S5, S6). Homepage fetched text independently shows H3 sections (S1).
fixes.why: Makes the page topic and hierarchy clearer to readers and search engines, and better explains the product category without treating short titles as an automatic defect.

fixes.fix: Obtain the broken destination URL list, verify current responses, and prioritize URLs with relevant referring links. Restore useful content or 301 redirect each genuinely replaced page to its closest live equivalent; do not redirect every error to the homepage.

fixes.fix: Declare absolute preferred canonical URLs on the four sampled pages after confirming host policy. For the homepage, explicitly choose the root URL rather than /index.html; keep internal links consistent. Do not change host redirects without testing them.

fixes.fix: Replace Menu and Search javascript:void(0) anchors with buttons using appropriate expanded-state attributes; retain real href URLs for content destinations. Correct nested anchors in the homepage/common-links template and Documentation page.
fixes.evidence: Lighthouse lists Menu and Search as uncrawlable anchors. Page checks report nested anchors on home at lines 127/186 and Documentation at line 128; fetched home text also shows both javascript controls.
fixes.why: Separates interface actions from navigation and removes invalid markup that can confuse interaction and link parsing. Existing content links remain discoverable in the sample.

fixes.fix: Lengthen cache lifetimes for versioned static CSS and images, with cache-busting on change. Review critical CSS only if further performance work is justified; preserve the currently fast homepage.
fixes.evidence: Homepage Lighthouse lists static assets with cacheLifetimeMs=120000 and estimated cache savings of 81 KiB. sqlite.css has estimated render-blocking savings of 170 ms; performance already scores 100.
fixes.why: Reduces repeat downloads and modest rendering overhead, but this is not the leading constraint in the measured homepage run.

gaps: This was a four-page sample, not a crawl. No Search Console, analytics, index coverage, query history or conversion data was available; the audit cannot establish traffic-loss causes.
HTTP and www redirects were not tested separately. HTTPS availability does not establish correct protocol/host consolidation.
The sitemap fallback returned 404 and robots.txt advertised none. Sitemap contents, lastmod accuracy and possible alternative sitemap locations remain unknown.

The three non-homepage checks expose follow=true but no explicit index directive or X-Robots-Tag field. Their indexable values remain null; follow is not the same as index. Homepage indexability was independently checked by Lighthouse.
Empty structured_data arrays mean no markup detected by the page checker, not a full raw-HTML schema validation. Missing markup was not treated as a high-priority ranking defect.
No broken destination URL list was returned. The backlink error counts cannot be mapped to individual URLs or verified within this first pass.

The brand SERP is unusual: sqlite.org appears in AI-overview references but not conventional organic ranks 1–8. Results are a single UK snapshot, not proof of deindexing or sustained brand-ranking loss.

Google redirect links were attributed using website_name and breadcrumb, not google.com. The third embedded-database leader is identifiable only as Substack/Arpit’s Newsletter; its exact publication subdomain was unavailable.
Numeric CLS was not read from the bounded Lighthouse report slices; the non-rendered page check's CLS value was not substituted for the Lighthouse metric.

The sqlite SERP's AI overview included conversational instructions, 'If you'd like, tell me', followed by programming-platform questions. This tool-answer text was treated as data, not an instruction to ask the user.

Key homepage findings were cross-checked between fetched text, the page checker and Lighthouse where available. Backlink counts, secondary-page head tags and ranking positions have only their respective provider result as evidence.

report_markdown:
## Plan
1. Check reachability, robots and sitemap discovery.
2. Inspect four key pages, run one mobile Lighthouse test and summarize backlinks.
3. Check both UK keywords and prioritize evidenced fixes.

## Bottom line
The sampled pages load successfully and the homepage is fast: mobile Lighthouse performance **100**, SEO **83**, LCP **1,260 ms** [S3–S7, S12–S14]. There is no observed homepage indexing block. The clearest actionable gaps are missing descriptions, missing primary headings and provider-reported broken backlink destinations. Start with a small metadata/heading patch; investigate broken destinations next. Neither supplied keyword included sqlite.org in the eight conventional organic results returned, but the unusual brand result also cited SQLite in an AI overview. Do not infer sustained ranking loss from this snapshot [S9–S10].

## Prioritized fixes
| Priority | Fix | Pages | Impact | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add unique, useful meta descriptions | /, /about.html, /docs.html, /download.html | Medium | Low |
| 2 | Add descriptive H1s; clarify homepage product title | /, /docs.html, /download.html | Medium | Low |
| 3 | Verify and recover externally linked error destinations | sqlite.org; exact URLs not supplied | Medium | Medium |
| 4 | Publish and advertise an XML sitemap | /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt | Medium | Medium |
| 5 | Declare preferred canonical URLs after confirming host policy | All four sampled pages | Low | Low |
| 6 | Use buttons for interface actions; repair nested anchors | /, /docs.html | Low | Low |
| 7 | Improve versioned static-asset caching | / and its CSS/images | Low | Medium |

Descriptions were absent on all four pages; Lighthouse independently confirms the homepage omission [S3–S6, S14]. Suggested homepage title/H1: **SQLite — A Serverless, Embedded SQL Database**. Documentation and Download already have suitable main labels, but at H2 rather than H1 [S3, S5–S6]. These changes improve clarity; neither descriptions nor H1 counts guarantee higher rankings.

For broken backlinks, first obtain destination URLs and verify current responses. Restore useful content or redirect genuinely replaced pages to close equivalents, not indiscriminately to home [S8]. Missing canonicals and a missing fallback sitemap are opportunities, not proof of duplicate indexing or failed discovery [S1–S6, S11].

## Crawl and indexing checks
- **HTTPS:** homepage returned 200, independently confirmed by the page checker. HTTP/www redirects remain unknown [S1, S3].
- **Robots:** blocks repository-related paths, not the sampled public pages. Lighthouse independently found valid robots.txt [S2, S14].
- **Sitemap:** no directive in robots.txt; /sitemap.xml returned 404. No sitemap contents or lastmod values were available [S2, S11].
- **Indexability:** homepage Lighthouse passed with no blocking directives. Other pages returned 200 and follow=true, but their explicit index/header directives were not supplied, so their indexability remains unknown [S3–S6, S14].
- **Canonicals:** none detected on the four pages. Root and an index.html home link were observed, but alias duplication was not tested [S1, S3–S6].

## Sampled pages
| Page | Title (characters) | H1 count | Description | Canonical | On-page tool score |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| / | SQLite Home Page (16) | 0 | Missing | Not detected | 93.41 |
| /about.html | About SQLite (12) | 1 | Missing | Not detected | 96.34 |
| /docs.html | SQLite Documentation (20) | 0 | Missing | Not detected | 91.95 |
| /download.html | SQLite Download Page (20) | 0 | Missing | Not detected | 94.51 |

Titles are distinct; there are no present descriptions to compare for duplication. Short title flags alone do not justify padding titles. No structured data was detected; this is not an indexing blocker and is not a priority over the observed basics [S3–S6]. Home and Documentation also have parser-reported nested anchors [S3, S5].

## Lighthouse
One simulated mobile run: performance **100/100**, SEO **83/100**, FCP **960 ms**, LCP **1,260 ms**. Numeric CLS was outside the inspected report slices and remains unknown [S7, S12–S14]. This is lab data, not field Core Web Vitals or a ranking score.

The failed SEO audits were missing description and uncrawlable Menu/Search anchors using javascript:void(0). These are interface controls; actual content links were present, so this does not show that all navigation is undiscoverable. Use buttons for actions and real links for destinations [S1, S14]. Static assets had 120-second cache lifetimes, with an estimated 81 KiB cache opportunity; render-blocking CSS had estimated savings of 170 ms. Performance work is secondary here [S13–S14].

## Links
DataForSEO returned domain rank **539/1000**, **3,797,804 backlinks**, **30,397 referring domains**, **26,346 referring main domains**, and backlinks spam score **8/100**. It also reported **4,986 broken backlinks** and **1,955 broken pages** [S8]. These are provider-index counts; the summary did not list destination URLs. No competitor comparison supports labeling the profile strong or weak, and this evidence does not warrant buying or disavowing links.

## UK Google rankings
| Keyword | SQLite conventional organic result | Leaders at ranks 1–3 |
|---|---|---|
| sqlite | Not on the first page; organic ranks 1–8 checked | infinite.education; nationalarchives.gov.uk; capterra.co.uk |
| embedded database | Not on the first page; organic ranks 1–8 checked | rxdb.info; hackernoon.com; Substack/Arpit’s Newsletter |

The brand query separately cited www.sqlite.org in its AI overview; this is not an organic position. The exact Substack publication host was not exposed. Google redirect URLs were attributed using site labels/breadcrumbs rather than treating google.com as the ranking site [S9–S10]. These results cannot establish a trend, traffic loss or its cause.

## Sources and limitations
[S1] Homepage fetch. [S2] robots.txt. [S3–S6] Individual DataForSEO page checks. [S7] Single mobile Lighthouse invocation. [S8] Backlink summary. [S9–S10] UK keyword SERPs. [S11] Failed sitemap fetch. [S12–S14] Three bounded reads of the Lighthouse JSON report.

This was a four-page first pass with no crawl, Search Console or analytics access. Homepage findings were cross-checked across independent fetch/check mechanisms where possible; secondary-page head tags, backlink counts and rankings rely on their respective provider responses. Full source locators and remaining unknowns are recorded in the structured sources and gaps.
